newsitem.title: UK: Britain welcomes Holbrooke Cyprus appointment.
newsitem.headline: Britain welcomes Holbrooke Cyprus appointment.

text.p: Britain praised the appointment of Bosnian mediator Richard Holbrooke as a special U.S. emissary for Cyprus on Wednesday, saying his wealth of experience would be helpful in resolving the problems of the divided island.
"We welcome the appointment," a foreign office spokesman said.

"A concerted international effort to get a comprehensive solution to the Cyprus problem is a high priority. We look forward to working closely with him in support of the UN secretary general's mission of good offices."
President Bill Clinton appointed Holbrooke to replace Richard Beattie who was named a special adviser to Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.
Holbrooke, a tough negotiator, won international praise for the 1995 Dayton peace agreement which ended the Bosnian civil war.
Cyprus, which gained its independence from Britain in 1960, has been divided since a Turkish invasion in 1974 in response to a pro-Greece coup.
In November 1983, the Turkish Cypriot parliament declared an independent "Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus" recognised only by Turkey.
President Glafkos Clerides of Cyprus and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash are due to meet in July in New York for their first face-to-face talks in nearly three years.
